summary: 40-foot pole tower with 7x7 cab built 1932 on Slumber Mountain; abandoned in the 1940s; photos show footings and debris; road gated.

facts.design: 40-foot pole tower with 7x7 cab and tent cabin
facts.status_note: Abandoned in the 1940s; the register lists it as gone, while WillhiteWeb photos show footings, a bedframe, the top of the cab roof and debris.

access.note: Road gated: closed December 1 to July 1 for wildlife habitat, and the upper gate is closed and blocked.

visit.trail_note: Short hike to a low, tree-covered summit; WillhiteWeb lists 2.5 miles round trip and 500 feet of gain.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Former Fire Lookout Sites register says the tower and tent cabin are now gone; WillhiteWeb photos show timber footings, a bedframe, part of the cab roof and debris. The story reports both: the structure is gone, and some remains are visible in the photographs.

notes_for_editor: Built date (1932) and abandonment (1940s) agree across three sources, and a 1932 newspaper quote corroborates the build. The 1935 fire comes from WillhiteWeb and a newspaper quote on the weebly page. The current condition rests on undated WillhiteWeb photo captions, so the story says what those show and not when they were taken. No staffing history was found. The 'patrol point' use is attributed by WillhiteWeb to Kresek and is undated, so it is not in the event list. Access is set to restricted because of the gates; no closure order was found. The 'ground building' in the photo caption is not identified as the tent cabin, and the story does not say it is.
